L1 → English

Your first language is evidence.

Transfer errors are not random failures. They often reveal a logical pattern from another language—and therefore point directly toward a useful English lesson.

Spanish

Spanish learners often transfer useful patterns, but English needs tighter control of auxiliaries, prepositions, articles, and word order.

para / por

Overusing for in English

Target: for, to, by, and because

conocer / saber

Mixing know a person and know a fact

Target: know, meet, and be familiar with

tener años

Saying I have 30 years

Target: age with be

no before verb

Dropping do in negatives

Target: do-support for negatives

Portuguese

Portuguese transfer work often focuses on false friends, prepositions, auxiliary choice, and deciding when English needs an explicit subject.

ficar

Choosing stay, become, get, or be

Target: ficar map into English

saudade / sentir falta

Choosing miss, miss out, or feel like

Target: miss and missing

tenho 25 anos

Age with have

Target: age with be

fazer perguntas

Make vs do confusion

Target: make, do, and ask

Turkish

Turkish learners often need explicit practice with articles, be, word order in questions, and tense/aspect choices that English marks differently.

no articles

Leaving out a, an, and the

Target: articles as meaning signals

subject-object-verb

Moving English verbs too late

Target: English word order

var / yok

Mapping existence to there is / there are

Target: there is and there are

one broad present

Choosing present simple or continuous

Target: routine vs happening now
